```{r karte}
# Daten laden
standorte <- readxl::read_excel("../../R/Arvato_Distributionsstandorte_Deutschland.xlsx")

# Automobilwerke in Norddeutschland und Benelux (Kunden / Bedarfsorte)
# Bekannte Werke in der Region: VW Wolfsburg, BMW Hannover,
# Mercedes Bremen, Daimler Düsseldorf, Volvo Gent, Audi Brüssel,
# VW Emden, Ford Köln, Opel Rüsselsheim
kunden <- data.frame(
  name = c(
    "VW Wolfsburg", "VW Emden", "BMW Hannover",
    "Mercedes Bremen", "Daimler Düsseldorf", "Ford Köln",

)

# Mögliche Lagerstandorte aus Arvato-Daten
# (Repräsentative Standorte aus Norddeutschland + Benelux)
if (exists("standorte") && "lat" %in% names(standorte) && "lon" %in% names(standorte)) {
```

## Problemstellung
Zur Versorgung der Automobilwerke in Norddeutschland und den Benelux-Ländern mit Antriebs-Batterien soll eine Versorgungskette aufgebaut werden. Ein bereits in der Automobilbranche tätiger Logistikdienstleister bietet an, die Versorgung der Werke mit Antriebs-Batterien zu übernehmen. Dazu müssen Investitionen in die Lagerstandorte getätigt werden, um die Regularien für Gefahrgutlagerung einzuhalten.

## Fallstudie - Batterielogistik
::: slide-subtitle
Aufgabe
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Zielformulierung

Sie wurden von ihrem Vorgesetzten aufgefordert eine Entscheidungsvorlage für erarbeiten, wie die Batteriedistribution organisiert werden könnte. Die Vorlage soll eine Zuordnung der Werke zu Versorgungslagern enthalten. Auf Basis dieser Zuordnung erwartet das Management eine Abschätzung der jährlichen Gesamtkosten, die aus Ihrem Vorschlag resultieren würden. Dies soll als Grundlage für ein Angebot und die Verhandlungen mit dem Automobilkonsortium dienen.
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
### Aufgaben

1. Formulieren Sie einen Ansatz zur Berechnung der jährlichen Gesamtkosten. 
2. Formulieren Sie einen Ansatz zur Berechnung der Transportkosten für die Batteriedistribution per LKW.
3. Ermitteln Sie dazu einen geeigneten Transportkostensatz für Batterien. 
4. Finden Sie eine Zuordnung der Werke zu den Lagerstandorten ermitteln Sie die Gesamtkosten Ihrer Lösung.
:::

## Warehouse Location Problem {#slide-wlp-1}
::: slide-subtitle
Problembeschreibung
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" icon=false}
**Problemstellung**

Gegeben sei eine Menge an **Kundenstandorten** und eine Menge (potentieller) **Lagerhausstandorte**. Jeder Kundenstandort hat eine **Warennachfrage** (z.B. in Stück pro Monat/Jahr), die von den Lagerhäusern beliefert warden muss. Der Transport der Waren verursacht entfernungsabhängige **Transportkosten**. Die Eröffnung eines Lagerhauses verursacht **Einrichtungskosten**.

Es ist zu entscheiden, an welchen Standorten Lagerhäuser eingerichtet werden sollen und welche Kunden diese versorgen sollen.
:::

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}

::: {.smaller-text}
::: {.fragment .fade-up}
**Notation**

- Menge der Lagerhäuser $i \in I$
- Menge der Kundenstandorte $j \in J$
- Transportverbindungen $E \subseteq I \times J$
- Eröffnungskosten an Lagerstandort $i$: $f_i$
- Transportkosten (z.B. in €/Monat) Standort $i$ zu Kunde $j$: $c_{ij}$
- Nachfrage von Kunde $j$: $a_j$
:::
:::
:::

::: {.column width="42%"}
::: {.fragment .fade-up}

```{r wlp-graph}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-width: "90%"
#| fig-height: 5

# --- Koordinaten (normiert 0..1) ---
lager <- data.frame(
  id  = c("W1","W2","W3"),
  lbl = c("1","2","3"),
  fi  = c("f<sub>1</sub>", "...", "f<sub>3</sub>"),
  x   = 0.20,
  y   = c(0.15, 0.50, 0.85)
)

kunden <- data.frame(
  id  = c("A","B","C","D"),
  lbl = c("A","B","C","D"),
  aj  = c("a<sub>A</sub>", "", "...", "a<sub>D</sub>"),
  x   = 0.75,
  y   = c(0.85, 0.60, 0.35, 0.10)
)

lxy <- setNames(lager[, c("x","y")],   c("x","y")); rownames(lxy) <- lager$id
kxy <- setNames(kunden[, c("x","y")],  c("x","y")); rownames(kxy) <- kunden$id

# Knotenradius in Plot-Koordinaten (angepasst an fig-Größe)
r <- 0.058   # <-- ggf. leicht anpassen wenn Größe ändert

edges <- data.frame(
  from = c("W3","W3","W2","W2","W2","W1"),
  to   = c("A", "B", "B", "C", "D", "D"),
  lbl  = c("c<sub>1A</sub>","","","","","c<sub>3D</sub>"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

fig <- plot_ly(type = "scatter", mode = "markers")

# Kanten: Endpunkte auf Rand der Knoten verschieben
for (i in seq_len(nrow(edges))) {
  x0 <- lxy[edges$from[i], "x"];  y0 <- lxy[edges$from[i], "y"]
  x1 <- kxy[edges$to[i],   "x"];  y1 <- kxy[edges$to[i],   "y"]

  dx <- x1 - x0;  dy <- y1 - y0
  d  <- sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2)

  # Startpunkt: r vom Lager-Mittelpunkt entfernt Richtung Kunde
  ax <- x0 + r * dx / d
  ay <- y0 + r * dy / d
  # Endpunkt:   r vom Kunden-Mittelpunkt entfernt Richtung Lager
  ex <- x1 - r * dx / d
  ey <- y1 - r * dy / d

  fig <- fig %>% add_annotations(
    x = ex, y = ey, ax = ax, ay = ay,
    xref = "x", yref = "y", axref = "x", ayref = "y",
    showarrow = TRUE, arrowhead = 2, arrowsize = 1,
    arrowwidth = 1.5, arrowcolor = "#4B4B4B", text = ""
  )

  # Kanten-Label mittig
  if (nchar(edges$lbl[i]) > 0) {
    fig <- fig %>% add_annotations(
      x = (ax + ex) / 2 + 0.02, y = (ay + ey) / 2 + 0.025,
      xref = "x", yref = "y",
      text = edges$lbl[i], showarrow = FALSE,
      font = list(size = 13, color = "#1F2933", family = "Arial")
    )
  }
}

# Lager-Knoten (Hexagon)
fig <- fig %>% add_trace(
  x = lager$x, y = lager$y, text = lager$lbl,
  mode = "markers+text",
  marker = list(symbol = "hexagon", size = 40,
                color = "#BFDBF7", line = list(color = "#4B5563", width = 1.5)),
  textfont = list(size = 16, color = "#1F2933", family = "Arial"),
  textposition = "middle center",
  hoverinfo = "skip", showlegend = FALSE
)

# f_i links
fig <- fig %>% add_annotations(
  x = lager$x - 0.10, y = lager$y,
  xref = "x", yref = "y",
  text = lager$fi, showarrow = FALSE,
  font = list(size = 14, color = "#1F2933", family = "Arial"),
  xanchor = "right"
)

# Kunden-Knoten (Circle)
fig <- fig %>% add_trace(
  x = kunden$x, y = kunden$y, text = kunden$lbl,
  mode = "markers+text",
  marker = list(symbol = "circle", size = 40,
                color = "#2D9E8E", line = list(color = "#2F3E46", width = 1.5)),
  textfont = list(size = 16, color = "white", family = "Arial"),
  textposition = "middle center",
  hoverinfo = "skip", showlegend = FALSE
)

# a_j rechts
fig <- fig %>% add_annotations(
  x = kunden$x + 0.08, y = kunden$y,
  xref = "x", yref = "y",
  text = kunden$aj, showarrow = FALSE,
  font = list(size = 14, color = "#1F2933", family = "Arial"),
  xanchor = "left"
)

# Set-Labels
fig <- fig %>% add_annotations(
  x = c(0.20, 0.75), y = c(1.00, 1.00),
  xref = "x", yref = "y",
  text = c("<b>Set <i>I</i></b>", "<b>Set <i>J</i></b>"),
  showarrow = FALSE,
  font = list(size = 14, color = "#1F2933", family = "Arial")
)

fig <- fig %>% layout(
  xaxis = list(visible = FALSE, range = c(0, 1), fixedrange = TRUE),
  yaxis = list(visible = FALSE, range = c(-0.05, 1.08), fixedrange = TRUE),
  plot_bgcolor  = "transparent",
  paper_bgcolor = "transparent",
  margin = list(l = 40, r = 40, t = 10, b = 10),
  height = 380
)

fig
```

## Warehouse Location Problem {#slide-wlp-model}
::: slide-subtitle
Mathematisches Modell
:::

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" icon=false}
#### Gemischt-ganzzahliges lineares Optimierungsmodell
Minimiere die Gesamtkosten aus Transport und Standorteröffnung

$$\min \rightarrow \sum_{i \in I} y_i \cdot f_i + \sum_{(i,j) \in E} x_{ij} \cdot c_{ij}$$
:::

::: {.smaller-text}

**Nebenbedingungen**
$$
\begin{align}
  \sum_{(i,j) \in E} x_{ij} &= a_j          & \forall j \in J      &\quad\rightarrow \text{Nachfrage befriedigen} \\
  x_{ij}                    &\leq y_i \cdot a_j & \forall (i,j) \in E &\quad\rightarrow \text{nur Transporte von eröffneten Standorten} \\
  x_{ij}                    &\geq 0          & \forall (i,j) \in E &\quad\rightarrow \text{Transportmengen nicht negativ} \\
  y_i                       &\in \{0,1\}     & \forall i \in I     &\quad\rightarrow \text{Standort wird eröffnet oder nicht}
\end{align}
$$
:::

:::
::: {.column width="43%"}

```{r wlp-graph2}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-width: "99%"
#| fig-height: 5

# --- Koordinaten (normiert 0..1) ---
lager <- data.frame(
  id  = c("W1","W2","W3"),
  lbl = c("1","2","3"),
  fi  = c("f<sub>1</sub>", "...", "f<sub>3</sub>"),
  x   = 0.20,
  y   = c(0.15, 0.50, 0.85)
)

kunden <- data.frame(
  id  = c("A","B","C","D"),
  lbl = c("A","B","C","D"),
  aj  = c("a<sub>A</sub>", "", "...", "a<sub>D</sub>"),
  x   = 0.75,
  y   = c(0.85, 0.60, 0.35, 0.10)
)

lxy <- setNames(lager[, c("x","y")],   c("x","y")); rownames(lxy) <- lager$id
kxy <- setNames(kunden[, c("x","y")],  c("x","y")); rownames(kxy) <- kunden$id

# Knotenradius in Plot-Koordinaten (angepasst an fig-Größe)
r <- 0.058   # <-- ggf. leicht anpassen wenn Größe ändert

edges <- data.frame(
  from = c("W3","W3","W2","W2","W2","W1"),
  to   = c("A", "B", "B", "C", "D", "D"),
  lbl  = c("c<sub>1A</sub>","","","","","c<sub>3D</sub>"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

fig <- plot_ly(type = "scatter", mode = "markers")

# Kanten: Endpunkte auf Rand der Knoten verschieben
for (i in seq_len(nrow(edges))) {
  x0 <- lxy[edges$from[i], "x"];  y0 <- lxy[edges$from[i], "y"]
  x1 <- kxy[edges$to[i],   "x"];  y1 <- kxy[edges$to[i],   "y"]

  dx <- x1 - x0;  dy <- y1 - y0
  d  <- sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2)

  # Startpunkt: r vom Lager-Mittelpunkt entfernt Richtung Kunde
  ax <- x0 + r * dx / d
  ay <- y0 + r * dy / d
  # Endpunkt:   r vom Kunden-Mittelpunkt entfernt Richtung Lager
  ex <- x1 - r * dx / d
  ey <- y1 - r * dy / d

  fig <- fig %>% add_annotations(
    x = ex, y = ey, ax = ax, ay = ay,
    xref = "x", yref = "y", axref = "x", ayref = "y",
    showarrow = TRUE, arrowhead = 2, arrowsize = 1,
    arrowwidth = 1.5, arrowcolor = "#4B4B4B", text = ""
  )

  # Kanten-Label mittig
  if (nchar(edges$lbl[i]) > 0) {
    fig <- fig %>% add_annotations(
      x = (ax + ex) / 2 + 0.02, y = (ay + ey) / 2 + 0.025,
      xref = "x", yref = "y",
      text = edges$lbl[i], showarrow = FALSE,
      font = list(size = 13, color = "#1F2933", family = "Arial")
    )
  }
}

# Lager-Knoten (Hexagon)
fig <- fig %>% add_trace(
  x = lager$x, y = lager$y, text = lager$lbl,
  mode = "markers+text",
  marker = list(symbol = "hexagon", size = 40,
                color = "#BFDBF7", line = list(color = "#4B5563", width = 1.5)),
  textfont = list(size = 16, color = "#1F2933", family = "Arial"),
  textposition = "middle center",
  hoverinfo = "skip", showlegend = FALSE
)

# f_i links
fig <- fig %>% add_annotations(
  x = lager$x - 0.10, y = lager$y,
  xref = "x", yref = "y",
  text = lager$fi, showarrow = FALSE,
  font = list(size = 14, color = "#1F2933", family = "Arial"),
  xanchor = "right"
)

# Kunden-Knoten (Circle)
fig <- fig %>% add_trace(
  x = kunden$x, y = kunden$y, text = kunden$lbl,
  mode = "markers+text",
  marker = list(symbol = "circle", size = 40,
                color = "#2D9E8E", line = list(color = "#2F3E46", width = 1.5)),
  textfont = list(size = 16, color = "white", family = "Arial"),
  textposition = "middle center",
  hoverinfo = "skip", showlegend = FALSE
)

# a_j rechts
fig <- fig %>% add_annotations(
  x = kunden$x + 0.08, y = kunden$y,
  xref = "x", yref = "y",
  text = kunden$aj, showarrow = FALSE,
  font = list(size = 14, color = "#1F2933", family = "Arial"),
  xanchor = "left"
)

# Set-Labels
fig <- fig %>% add_annotations(
  x = c(0.20, 0.75), y = c(1.00, 1.00),
  xref = "x", yref = "y",
  text = c("<b>Set <i>I</i></b>", "<b>Set <i>J</i></b>"),
  showarrow = FALSE,
  font = list(size = 14, color = "#1F2933", family = "Arial")
)

fig <- fig %>% layout(
  xaxis = list(visible = FALSE, range = c(0, 1), fixedrange = TRUE),
  yaxis = list(visible = FALSE, range = c(-0.05, 1.08), fixedrange = TRUE),
  plot_bgcolor  = "transparent",
  paper_bgcolor = "transparent",
  margin = list(l = 40, r = 40, t = 10, b = 10),
  height = 380
)

fig
```

## WLP – Kleines Fallbeispiel {#slide-wlp-example}
::: slide-subtitle
Probleminstanz (5 Lager, 6 Kunden)
:::

```{r wlp-example-data}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Problemdaten
wlp_lager <- data.frame(
  ID      = c("W1", "W2", "W3", "W4", "W5"),
  fi      = c(110,  95, 140,  80, 125),   # Eröffnungskosten (T€/Jahr)
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

wlp_kunden <- data.frame(
  ID  = c("C1", "C2", "C3", "C4", "C5", "C6"),
  aj  = c(40,   25,   60,   30,   50,   35),   # Nachfrage (Einheiten)
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Transportkosten cij (T€ je Einheit × km, bereits als Gesamtkosten pro Jahr)
wlp_cij <- matrix(
  c(1.8, 3.2, 2.5, 4.1, 1.2, 3.7,
    3.4, 1.1, 3.8, 1.6, 2.9, 2.2,
    2.6, 4.0, 1.3, 3.5, 3.1, 1.9,
    4.2, 1.8, 2.9, 1.0, 3.6, 2.7,
    1.5, 3.6, 3.3, 4.4, 2.0, 1.4),
  nrow = 5, byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(wlp_lager$ID, wlp_kunden$ID)
)
```

::: columns
::: {.column width="38%"}

::: small-text
**Lager – Eröffnungskosten $f_i$ (T€/Jahr)**

```{r}
#| echo: false
kbl(wlp_lager,
    col.names = c("Lager $i$", "$f_i$ (T€)"),
    align = c("c","r"), escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("condensed","striped"),
                full_width = TRUE, font_size = 18) |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, background = "#2F3E46", color = "white") |>
  row_spec(0, background = "#2F3E46", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
```

**Kunden – Nachfrage $a_j$ (Einheiten/Jahr)**

```{r}
#| echo: false
kbl(wlp_kunden,
    col.names = c("Kunde $j$", "$a_j$"),
    align = c("c","r"), escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("condensed","striped"),
                full_width = TRUE, font_size = 18) |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, background = "#2D9E8E", color = "white") |>
  row_spec(0, background = "#2D9E8E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
```
:::

:::
::: {.column width="59%"}

::: small-text
**Transportkosten $c_{ij}$ (T€/Einheit · Jahr)**

```{r}
#| echo: false
kbl(as.data.frame(wlp_cij),
    align = rep("r", 6), escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("condensed","striped"),
                full_width = TRUE, font_size = 18) |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, background = "#2F3E46", color = "white") |>
  row_spec(0, background = "#2F3E46", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**Gesamtkosten** = Eröffnungskosten der gewählten Lager  
$\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad$ + Transportkosten × Nachfrage je Zuordnung  
$$Z = \sum_{i} y_i f_i + \sum_{i,j} x_{ij} \cdot c_{ij}$$
:::

## WLP – Lösung mit R/OMPR {#slide-wlp-ompr}
::: slide-subtitle
Implementierung als MILP
:::

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}

```{r wlp-ompr-code}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-line-numbers: true

library(ompr)
library(ompr.roi)
library(ROI.plugin.glpk)

# Problemdaten
n_I <- 5; n_J <- 6
f   <- c(110, 95, 140, 80, 125)
a   <- c(40, 25, 60, 30, 50, 35)
c_ij <- matrix(
  c(1.8,3.2,2.5,4.1,1.2,3.7,
    3.4,1.1,3.8,1.6,2.9,2.2,
    2.6,4.0,1.3,3.5,3.1,1.9,
    4.2,1.8,2.9,1.0,3.6,2.7,
    1.5,3.6,3.3,4.4,2.0,1.4),
  nrow = n_I, byrow = TRUE)

# MILP-Modell
model <- MIPModel() |>
  # Variablen
  add_variable(y[i], i = 1:n_I, type = "binary") |>
  add_variable(x[i,j], i = 1:n_I, j = 1:n_J,
               type = "continuous", lb = 0) |>
  # Zielfunktion
  set_objective(
    sum_expr(f[i] * y[i], i = 1:n_I) +
    sum_expr(c_ij[i,j] * x[i,j],
             i = 1:n_I, j = 1:n_J),
    sense = "min") |>
  # NB1: Nachfrage vollständig befriedigen
  add_constraint(
    sum_expr(x[i,j], i = 1:n_I) == a[j],
    j = 1:n_J) |>
  # NB2: Transport nur von eröffneten Lagern
  add_constraint(
    x[i,j] <= y[i] * a[j],
    i = 1:n_I, j = 1:n_J)

result <- solve_model(model,
           with_ROI(solver = "glpk", verbose = FALSE))
```

:::
::: {.column width="42%"}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## OMPR – Workflow

1. `MIPModel()` → leeres Modell
2. `add_variable()` → Entscheidungsvariablen
3. `set_objective()` → Zielfunktion
4. `add_constraint()` → Nebenbedingungen
5. `solve_model()` → Solver aufrufen
6. `get_solution()` → Lösung extrahieren
:::

```{r wlp-ompr-result}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Optimale Lösung extrahieren
y_sol <- get_solution(result, y[i])
x_sol <- get_solution(result, x[i,j])

# Geöffnete Lager
offene_lager <- y_sol$i[y_sol$value > 0.5]

# Optimaler Zielfunktionswert
obj_val <- objective_value(result)
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**Optimaler Zielfunktionswert:**  
```{r}
#| echo: false
cat(paste0("Z* = ", round(obj_val, 1), " T€/Jahr"))
```
**Geöffnete Lager:** W`r paste(offene_lager, collapse = ", W")`
:::

:::
:::

## Heuristische Lösungsverfahren {#slide-heuristics-intro}
::: slide-subtitle
Motivation und Überblick
:::

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## Warum Heuristiken?

Das WLP ist **NP-schwer**: exakte Solver (MILP) finden zwar optimale Lösungen, aber die Rechenzeit wächst exponentiell mit $|I|$ und $|J|$. Für große Praxisinstanzen sind **konstruktive Heuristiken** oft der einzig praktikable Ansatz.
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
### Zwei klassische Ansätze

| Methode | Ausgangspunkt | Richtung |
|---|---|---|
| **Add-Heuristik** | Keine Lager offen | Schrittweise hinzufügen |
| **Drop-Heuristik** | Alle Lager offen | Schrittweise schließen |

- Jeder Schritt: **greedy** – wähle die Änderung mit der größten Kostenreduktion
- Abbruch, wenn keine weitere Verbesserung möglich
- Kunden werden stets dem **billigsten offenen Lager** zugeordnet
:::

:::
::: {.column width="42%"}

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
```{r heuristic-overview-plot}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-width: "99%"
#| fig-height: 5

# Schematische Kostenkurve: Add- vs. Drop-Verlauf
n_steps <- 5
steps   <- 0:n_steps

# Grobe Illustration (nicht exakte Werte)
cost_add  <- c(NA, 724.5, 639.5, rep(NA, 3))
cost_drop <- c(854.5, 759.0, 681.5, 641.5, rep(NA, 2))
cost_opt  <- rep(639.5, n_steps + 1)

df_plot <- data.frame(
  lager_offen = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 4, 3, 2),
  kosten      = c(724.5, 639.5, 854.5, 759.0, 681.5, NA, NA, NA, 641.5),
  methode     = c("Add","Add","Drop","Drop","Drop",NA,NA,NA,"Drop")
)

fig_h <- plot_ly()

# Add-Kurve
fig_h <- fig_h %>% add_trace(
  x = c(1, 2), y = c(724.5, 639.5),
  type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
  name = "Add-Heuristik",
  line   = list(color = "#01696f", width = 2.5),
  marker = list(color = "#01696f", size = 10)
)

# Drop-Kurve
fig_h <- fig_h %>% add_trace(
  x = c(5, 4, 3, 2), y = c(854.5, 759.0, 681.5, 641.5),
  type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
  name = "Drop-Heuristik",
  line   = list(color = "#da7101", width = 2.5, dash = "dash"),
  marker = list(color = "#da7101", size = 10)
)

# Optimum
fig_h <- fig_h %>% add_trace(
  x = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), y = rep(639.5, 5),
  type = "scatter", mode = "lines",
  name = "Optimum (Z* = 639,5)",
  line = list(color = "#a12c7b", width = 1.5, dash = "dot")
)

fig_h <- fig_h %>% layout(
  xaxis = list(title = "Anzahl offener Lager", dtick = 1,
               range = c(0.5, 5.5)),
  yaxis = list(title = "Gesamtkosten (T€/Jahr)",
               range = c(600, 900)),
  legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2),
  plot_bgcolor  = "transparent",
  paper_bgcolor = "transparent",
  margin = list(l = 50, r = 20, t = 10, b = 60),
  height = 340
)

fig_h
```

## Add-Heuristik {#slide-add-heuristic}
::: slide-subtitle
Algorithmus
:::

::: columns
::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" icon=false}
**Idee:** Starte ohne geöffnetes Lager. Füge in jedem Schritt dasjenige Lager $i^*$ hinzu, das die Gesamtkosten am stärksten **reduziert**.
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
### Algorithmus

**Initialisierung:** $S \leftarrow \emptyset$

**Wiederhole:**

1. Berechne für jedes noch nicht geöffnete Lager $i \notin S$ den Kostenbeitrag:
$$\Delta_i = Z(S) - Z(S \cup \{i\})$$

2. Wähle $i^* = \arg\max_{i \notin S} \Delta_i$

3. **Falls** $\Delta_{i^*} > 0$: öffne $i^*$, setze $S \leftarrow S \cup \{i^*\}$

4. **Sonst:** Abbruch

**Zuordnungsregel:** Jeder Kunde $j$ wird dem günstigsten offenen Lager zugeordnet:
$$\sigma(j) = \arg\min_{i \in S} c_{ij}$$
:::

:::
::: {.column width="46%"}

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Kostenberechnung

$$Z(S) = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in S} f_i}_{\text{Eröffnung}} + \underbrace{\sum_{j \in J} \min_{i \in S} c_{ij} \cdot a_j}_{\text{Transport}}$$

- **Laufzeit:** $\mathcal{O}(|I|^2 \cdot |J|)$  
- **Eigenschaft:** Greedy, nicht garantiert optimal
- **Stärke:** Berücksichtigt Synergien – ein neues Lager kann mehrere Kunden gleichzeitig günstiger versorgen
:::
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## Abbruchbedingung

Die Heuristik stoppt, sobald **kein** weiteres Lager die Gesamtkosten senkt – d.h. die Einsparung bei den Transportkosten die Eröffnungskosten des nächsten Lagers nicht mehr übersteigt.
:::
:::

:::
:::

---

## Drop-Heuristik {#slide-drop-heuristic}
::: slide-subtitle
Algorithmus
:::

::: columns
::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" icon=false}
**Idee:** Starte mit **allen** Lagern geöffnet. Schließe in jedem Schritt dasjenige Lager $i^*$, dessen Schließung die Gesamtkosten am stärksten **reduziert**.
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
### Algorithmus

**Initialisierung:** $S \leftarrow I$

**Wiederhole:**

1. Berechne für jedes noch geöffnete Lager $i \in S$ den Kostenbeitrag:
$$\Delta_i = Z(S) - Z(S \setminus \{i\})$$

2. Wähle $i^* = \arg\max_{i \in S} \Delta_i$

3. **Falls** $\Delta_{i^*} > 0$: schließe $i^*$, setze $S \leftarrow S \setminus \{i^*\}$

4. **Sonst:** Abbruch

**Zuordnungsregel:** identisch zur Add-Heuristik:
$$\sigma(j) = \arg\min_{i \in S} c_{ij}$$
:::

:::
::: {.column width="46%"}

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Vergleich mit Add-Heuristik

| Merkmal | Add | Drop |
|---|---|---|
| **Start** | $S = \emptyset$ | $S = I$ |
| **Richtung** | aufbauend | abbauend |
| **Startkosten** | $\infty$ (kein Lager) | $\sum_i f_i + \ldots$ |
| **Laufzeit** | $\mathcal{O}(|I|^2 \cdot |J|)$ | $\mathcal{O}(|I|^2 \cdot |J|)$ |
| **Tendenz** | wenige Lager | evtl. mehr Lager |

:::
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## Wichtig

Beide Heuristiken sind **nicht garantiert optimal**. Sie liefern zulässige Lösungen, die je nach Instanz nahe am Optimum oder deutlich davon entfernt sein können. Die Lösungsqualität hängt stark von der Kostenstruktur der Instanz ab.
:::
:::

:::
:::

## Add-Heuristik – Fallbeispiel {#slide-add-example}
::: slide-subtitle
Schrittweise Lösung der Probleminstanz
:::

```{r add-heuristic-compute}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Problemdaten (identisch zu slide-wlp-example)
n_I  <- 5; n_J <- 6
f_h  <- c(110, 95, 140, 80, 125)
a_h  <- c(40, 25, 60, 30, 50, 35)
c_h  <- matrix(
  c(1.8, 3.2, 2.5, 4.1, 1.2, 3.7,
    3.4, 1.1, 3.8, 1.6, 2.9, 2.2,
    2.6, 4.0, 1.3, 3.5, 3.1, 1.9,
    4.2, 1.8, 2.9, 1.0, 3.6, 2.7,
    1.5, 3.6, 3.3, 4.4, 2.0, 1.4),
  nrow = n_I, byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(paste0("W", 1:n_I), paste0("C", 1:n_J))
)

total_cost_h <- function(S) {
  if (length(S) == 0) return(Inf)
  sum(f_h[S]) + sum(sapply(1:n_J, function(j) min(c_h[S, j]) * a_h[j]))
}

best_assign <- function(S) {
  sapply(1:n_J, function(j) S[which.min(c_h[S, j])])
}

# Add-Heuristik durchführen
S_add_h  <- integer(0)
rem_h    <- 1:n_I
add_log  <- list()

repeat {
  cur_cost <- total_cost_h(S_add_h)
  gains <- sapply(rem_h, function(i) cur_cost - total_cost_h(c(S_add_h, i)))
  best_idx  <- which.max(gains)
  best_gain <- gains[best_idx]
  best_i    <- rem_h[best_idx]
  if (best_gain <= 0) break
  S_add_h  <- c(S_add_h, best_i)
  rem_h    <- setdiff(rem_h, best_i)
  asgn     <- best_assign(S_add_h)
  fix_cost <- sum(f_h[S_add_h])
  tr_cost  <- total_cost_h(S_add_h) - fix_cost
  add_log[[length(add_log)+1]] <- list(
    step      = length(add_log)+1,
    added     = best_i,
    open      = S_add_h,
    gain      = best_gain,
    fix       = fix_cost,
    transp    = tr_cost,
    total     = total_cost_h(S_add_h),
    assign    = asgn
  )
}
```

::: columns
::: {.column width="52%"}

::: small-text

```{r add-steps-table}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

add_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(add_log, function(s) {
  data.frame(
    Schritt    = s$step,
    Aktion     = paste0("+W", s$added),
    Offen      = paste0("{", paste0("W", sort(s$open), collapse=", "), "}"),
    Fix        = s$fix,
    Transport  = round(s$transp, 1),
    Gesamt     = round(s$total, 1),
    Zuordnung  = paste0(paste0("C", 1:n_J, "→W", s$assign), collapse=", ")
  )
}))

kbl(add_df[, c("Schritt","Aktion","Offen","Fix","Transport","Gesamt")],
    col.names = c("Schritt","Aktion","Offene Lager",
                  "Eröffn. (T€)","Transport (T€)","Gesamt (T€)"),
    align = c("c","c","l","r","r","r")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("condensed","striped"),
                full_width = TRUE, font_size = 16) |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, background = "#2F3E46", color = "white") |>
  column_spec(2, bold = TRUE, color = "#01696f") |>
  column_spec(6, bold = TRUE) |>
  row_spec(0, background = "#2F3E46", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
```


```{r add-solution-plot}
final_asgn_add <- best_assign(final_open_add)

lp_add <- data.frame(
  id   = paste0("W", 1:n_I),

  y    = c(0.08, 0.30, 0.52, 0.74, 0.92),

)

  id = paste0("C", 1:n_J),

lxy_a <- setNames(lp_add[, c("x","y")], c("x","y")); rownames(lxy_a) <- lp_add$id
kxy_a <- setNames(kp_add[, c("x","y")], c("x","y")); rownames(kxy_a) <- kp_add$id
r_a <- 0.048

fig_a <- plot_ly(type = "scatter", mode = "markers")

for (ii in 1:n_I) for (jj in 1:n_J) {
  wi <- paste0("W", ii); cj <- paste0("C", jj)
  x0 <- lxy_a[wi,"x"]; y0 <- lxy_a[wi,"y"]
  x1 <- kxy_a[cj,"x"]; y1 <- kxy_a[cj,"y"]
  dx <- x1-x0; dy <- y1-y0; dd <- sqrt(dx^2+dy^2)
  ax <- x0+r_a*dx/dd; ay <- y0+r_a*dy/dd
  ex <- x1-r_a*dx/dd; ey <- y1-r_a*dy/dd
  fig_a <- fig_a %>% add_annotations(
    x=ex,y=ey,ax=ax,ay=ay,xref="x",yref="y",axref="x",ayref="y",
    showarrow=TRUE,arrowhead=0,arrowsize=0.8,arrowwidth=0.8,
    arrowcolor="#D0D5DD",text="")
}

for (jj in 1:n_J) {
  wi <- paste0("W", final_asgn_add[jj]); cj <- paste0("C", jj)
  x0 <- lxy_a[wi,"x"]; y0 <- lxy_a[wi,"y"]
  x1 <- kxy_a[cj,"x"]; y1 <- kxy_a[cj,"y"]
  dx <- x1-x0; dy <- y1-y0; dd <- sqrt(dx^2+dy^2)
  ax <- x0+r_a*dx/dd; ay <- y0+r_a*dy/dd
  ex <- x1-r_a*dx/dd; ey <- y1-r_a*dy/dd
  fig_a <- fig_a %>% add_annotations(
    x=ex,y=ey,ax=ax,ay=ay,xref="x",yref="y",axref="x",ayref="y",
    showarrow=TRUE,arrowhead=2,arrowsize=1,arrowwidth=2.2,
    arrowcolor="#01696f",text="")
}

lc <- ifelse(lp_add$open, "#BFDBF7", "#E8E8E8")
lb <- ifelse(lp_add$open, "#4B5563", "#B0B0B0")
fig_a <- fig_a %>% add_trace(
  x=lp_add$x, y=lp_add$y, text=lp_add$id,
  mode="markers+text",
  marker=list(symbol="hexagon",size=38,color=lc,line=list(color=lb,width=2)),
  textfont=list(size=14,color="#1F2933",family="Arial"),
  textposition="middle center",hoverinfo="skip",showlegend=FALSE)
fig_a <- fig_a %>% add_annotations(
  x=lp_add$x-0.09, y=lp_add$y, xref="x",yref="y",
  text=ifelse(lp_add$open, paste0("f=",f_h,"✓"), paste0("f=",f_h)),
  showarrow=FALSE,
  font=list(size=11,color=ifelse(lp_add$open,"#01696f","#9CA3AF"),family="Arial"),
  xanchor="right")
fig_a <- fig_a %>% add_trace(
```

## Drop-Heuristik – Fallbeispiel {#slide-drop-example}
::: slide-subtitle
Schrittweise Lösung der Probleminstanz
:::

```{r drop-heuristic-compute}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

S_drop_h  <- 1:n_I
drop_log  <- list()

# Startzeile
fix0   <- sum(f_h[S_drop_h])
tr0    <- total_cost_h(S_drop_h) - fix0
drop_log[[1]] <- list(
  step    = 0,
  removed = NA,
  open    = S_drop_h,
  gain    = NA,
  fix     = fix0,
  transp  = tr0,
  total   = total_cost_h(S_drop_h),
  assign  = best_assign(S_drop_h)
)

repeat {
  if (length(S_drop_h) <= 1) break
  cur_cost <- total_cost_h(S_drop_h)
  gains <- sapply(S_drop_h, function(i)
    cur_cost - total_cost_h(setdiff(S_drop_h, i)))
  best_idx  <- which.max(gains)
  best_gain <- gains[best_idx]
  best_i    <- S_drop_h[best_idx]
  if (best_gain <= 0) break
  S_drop_h <- setdiff(S_drop_h, best_i)
  fix_cost <- sum(f_h[S_drop_h])
  tr_cost  <- total_cost_h(S_drop_h) - fix_cost
  asgn     <- best_assign(S_drop_h)
  drop_log[[length(drop_log)+1]] <- list(
    step    = length(drop_log),
    removed = best_i,
    open    = S_drop_h,
    gain    = best_gain,
    fix     = fix_cost,
    transp  = tr_cost,
    total   = total_cost_h(S_drop_h),
    assign  = asgn
  )
}
```

## Lösungsvergleich {#slide-heuristic-comparison}
::: slide-subtitle
Optimum vs. Add-Heuristik vs. Drop-Heuristik
:::

```{r comparison-compute}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Alle Lösungsdaten zusammenführen
cost_opt_val  <- total_cost_h(c(1, 2))     # W1, W2 – optimale Lösung (MILP)
cost_add_val  <- total_cost_h(S_add_h)
cost_drop_val <- total_cost_h(S_drop_h)

fix_opt  <- sum(f_h[c(1, 2)])
tr_opt   <- cost_opt_val  - fix_opt
fix_add  <- sum(f_h[S_add_h])
tr_add   <- cost_add_val  - fix_add
fix_drop <- sum(f_h[S_drop_h])
tr_drop  <- cost_drop_val - fix_drop

asgn_opt  <- best_assign(c(1, 2))
asgn_add  <- best_assign(S_add_h)
asgn_drop <- best_assign(S_drop_h)

gap_add  <- round((cost_add_val  / cost_opt_val - 1) * 100, 2)
gap_drop <- round((cost_drop_val / cost_opt_val - 1) * 100, 2)
```

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}

```{r comparison-table}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

comp_df <- data.frame(
  Kennzahl = c(
    "Geöffnete Lager",
    "Anzahl Lager",
    "Eröffnungskosten (T€)",
    "Transportkosten (T€)",
    "**Gesamtkosten Z (T€)**",
    "Gap zum Optimum (%)"
  ),
  Optimum = c(
    paste0("W", sort(c(1,2)), collapse=", "),
    length(c(1, 2)),
    fix_opt,
    round(tr_opt, 1),
    paste0("**", round(cost_opt_val, 1), "**"),
    "–"
  ),
  Add = c(
    paste0("W", sort(S_add_h), collapse=", "),
    length(S_add_h),
    fix_add,
    round(tr_add, 1),
    paste0("**", round(cost_add_val, 1), "**"),
    paste0(gap_add, " %")
  ),
  Drop = c(
    paste0("W", sort(S_drop_h), collapse=", "),
    length(S_drop_h),
    fix_drop,
    round(tr_drop, 1),
    paste0("**", round(cost_drop_val, 1), "**"),
    paste0(gap_drop, " %")
  )
)

kbl(comp_df,
    col.names = c("Kennzahl", "Optimum (MILP)", "Add-Heuristik", "Drop-Heuristik"),
    align = c("l","c","c","c"), escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("condensed","striped"),
                full_width = TRUE, font_size = 17) |>
  column_spec(1, bold = FALSE) |>
  column_spec(2, bold = TRUE, background = "#a12c7b", color = "white") |>
  column_spec(3, background = "#E8F4F1") |>
  column_spec(4, background = "#FEF3E2") |>
  row_spec(0, background = "#2F3E46", color = "white", bold = TRUE) |>
  row_spec(5, bold = TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
In diesem Fallbeispiel findet die **Add-Heuristik** zufällig die **optimale Lösung** ($Z = `r round(cost_add_val,1)`$ T€). Die **Drop-Heuristik** liefert mit $Z = `r round(cost_drop_val,1)`$ T€ eine um `r gap_drop` % schlechtere Lösung.
:::

:::
::: {.column width="48%"}

```{r comparison-bar}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-width: "99%"
#| fig-height: 5

methoden  <- c("Optimum (MILP)", "Add-Heuristik", "Drop-Heuristik")
fix_vals  <- c(fix_opt,  fix_add,  fix_drop)
tr_vals   <- c(round(tr_opt,1), round(tr_add,1), round(tr_drop,1))
farben_fix <- c("#a12c7b", "#01696f", "#da7101")
farben_tr  <- c("#d163a7", "#4f98a3", "#fdab43")

fig_bar <- plot_ly()

fig_bar <- fig_bar %>% add_trace(
  x = methoden, y = fix_vals, type = "bar", name = "Eröffnungskosten",
  marker = list(color = farben_fix),
  text = paste0(fix_vals, " T€"), textposition = "inside",
  insidetextanchor = "middle",
  textfont = list(color = "white", size = 13, family = "Arial")
)

fig_bar <- fig_bar %>% add_trace(
  x = methoden, y = tr_vals, type = "bar", name = "Transportkosten",
  marker = list(color = farben_tr),
  text = paste0(tr_vals, " T€"), textposition = "inside",
  insidetextanchor = "middle",
  textfont = list(color = "white", size = 13, family = "Arial")
)

# Gesamtkosten-Label oben
total_vals <- fix_vals + tr_vals
fig_bar <- fig_bar %>% add_annotations(
  x = methoden, y = total_vals + 12,
  text = paste0("<b>", total_vals, " T€</b>"),
  showarrow = FALSE,
  font = list(size = 14, color = "#1F2933", family = "Arial")
)

fig_bar <- fig_bar %>% layout(
  barmode = "stack",
  xaxis   = list(title = ""),
  yaxis   = list(title = "Kosten (T€/Jahr)", range = c(0, max(total_vals) * 1.15)),
  legend  = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.18),
  plot_bgcolor  = "transparent",
  paper_bgcolor = "transparent",
  margin = list(l = 50, r = 20, t = 30, b = 60),
  height = 380
)

fig_bar
```

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
**Allgemein gilt:** Heuristiken sind **nicht garantiert optimal**. Die Güte hängt von der Kostenstruktur ab. Für Praxisinstanzen mit $|I|, |J| \gg 100$ sind sie dennoch oft die einzig praktikable Alternative zu exakten Solvern.
:::
